followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: which model is likely to produce the better answer, and which model is suited to the query's style.

On capability, Dunlin edges out Plover across the board — MMLU-Pro (79.6 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (61.8 vs 56.2), and Support Dialogue (85.7 vs 78.9). The Support Dialogue gap especially matters since this is a friendly, person-to-person question rather than a dry data task.

On fit, the query is a warm, collaborative exchange — casual tone, a personal "I'd love your take," and a compliment. Dunlin self-reports a clear preference for exactly that kind of interaction (warm, collaborative exchanges at 63; open-ended generative work at 74). Plover, by contrast, leans toward well-specified extraction/transform and neutral transactional requests, and actively disprefers open-ended work (35).

So both signals pointed the same way: Dunlin is the stronger general explainer and the better tonal match. There was no extraction/transform element that would have favored Plover, so it was a fairly clean call.
